content.title: Braylon Mullins' otherworldly shot lifts UConn basketball to Final 4
content.text: Updated March 29, 2026, 8:12 p.m. ETThe sideline celebration nearly tore Dan Hurley's suit jacket off his shoulders when the shot went down.Braylon Mullins, you are a March Madness hero.The freshman combo-guard released a gutsy 3-pointer from several strides behind the line with 0.4 seconds left to seal the UConn men's basketball team's miraculous 73-72 victory over top-seeded Duke in Washington D.C. on Sunday, March 29.Hurley's Huskies, which completed a 19-point comeback, march on to play 3-seed Illinois in the Final Four in Indianapolis on Saturday, April 4 at 6 p.m.Mullins concluded the game with 10 points, and his golden shot flipped the Huskies' 3-point fate after the team started 1-for-18 from range (finished 5-for-23).See below for play-by-play score updates from the UConn vs. Duke thriller.FINAL: UConn 73, Duke 72Braylon Mullins goes down as an immortal March Madness hero. The freshman buried the game-winning 3-pointer from just inside the March Madness logo at mid-court to dethrone Duke and push UConn to the Final Four.The Huskies overcome a 19-point deficit. The winning shot was Mullins' only 3-point hit of the game (1-for-5). UConn's 3-point fortunes flipped after a 1-for-18 start from long range (finished 5-for-23).Tarris Reed Jr. led UConn with 26 points, 9 rebounds and 4 blocks. Silas Demary Jr. (11) and Solo Ball (10) also tallied double-digit points for the Huskies. Alex Karaban (5 points, 2-for-10 shooting) hit a crucial 3-pointer in the second half.For Duke, Cameron Boozer recorded 27 points, 8 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 blocks. Cayden Boozer had 15 points, 6 assists and 5 rebounds, Dame Sarr scored 10 points and Isaiah Evans scored 7.Braylon Mullins, an otherworldly 3-pointerUConn 73, Duke 72 -- 0.4 seconds, second half: The freshman uncorks a gutsy 3-pointer from a few strides behind the 3-point line to put UConn ahead inside the final second. Silas Demary Jr.'s deflection created a turnover by Duke's Cayden Boozer. Duke's 19-point lead is officially erased.Silas Demary Jr. splits free throwsDuke 72, UConn 70 -- 10 seconds, second half: The junior guard hits 1 of 2 free throws.Cameron Boozer scores for DukeDuke 72, UConn 69 -- 27.2 seconds, second half: Boozer converts to reinstate a 3-point edge for Duke. Timeout UConn.Alex Karaban drills a 3-pointer for UConnDuke 70, UConn 69 -- 45 seconds, second half: Alex Karaban, who was in the midst of a 1-for-9 shooting rut, knocks down a crucial 3-pointer from way beyond the line on the left wing. Tarris Reed Jr. set the screen.Timeout DukeDuke 70, UConn 66 -- 1:20 second half: The Blue Devils bring it across half-court and call timeout to regroup.Solo Ball fouled for UConnDuke 70, UConn 66 -- 1:31 second half: Ball snatches an offensive rebound and is fouled. He splits the two free throw attempts.Tarris Reed Jr., Solo Ball are second-half playmakers for UConnDuke 67, UConn 65 -- 3:42 second half: The Huskies' rally is roaring. A finish inside by Reed Jr. sliced the deficit to five, meanwhile Ball picks up a steal on one end and converts an and-one layup on the other.Reed Jr. has 26 points, 8 rebounds and 4 blocks. Ball has 8 points, 2 assists and 2 steals. UConn once trailed by 19.Silas Demary Jr. strikes gold from 3-point landDuke 65, UConn 58 -- 6:06 second half: The junior combo guard hits consecutive 3-pointers from the corner to restore UConn's fortunes from long range -- the team is 3-for-20 from distance on the game. Demary Jr. has 10 points for the Huskies.Cameron Boozer powers inside for DukeDuke 60, UConn 51 -- 7:59 second half: The Duke freshman lowers his shoulder into the chest of UConn's Braylon Mullins and lays it up for 2 after a goaltending call on UConn's Tarris Reed Jr. UConn coach Dan Hurley is pleading that an offensive foul should've been charged to Boozer.Jayden Ross, a key defensive strip for UConnDuke 58, UConn 49 -- 9:58 second half: Timeout is called as UConn's Jayden Ross strips the ball out of the grasp of Duke's Caleb Foster, and it deflects off the Blue Devils last.UConn making a second-half pushDuke 56, UConn 49 -- 10:59 second half: Tarris Reed Jr. slams down a dunk to cut the deficit to seven points. The Huskies are on a 16-6 run. Reed Jr. has 23 points, 5 rebounds and 4 blocks.Karaban is on the board for UConnDuke 56, UConn 47 -- 12:15 second half: The Huskies' captain is on the board. Alex Karaban received a bounce pass from Tarris Reed Jr on the interior to slice the deficit to single digits.Boozer, Boozer connect again for DukeDuke 55, UConn 41 -- 13:50 second half: Cameron Boozer rolls to the rim and receives a pass from his twin brother Cayden to throw down a dunk. Cameron Boozer has 18 points.And-one for UConn's Braylon MullinsDuke 50, UConn 36 -- 16:57 second half: The freshman forward has now hit two straight mid-range jumpers from the baseline in front of the Huskies' bench. He hits on the free throw and has 7 points.Silas Demary Jr. draws charge for UConnDuke 46, UConn 31 -- 18:20 second half: Duke's Cameron Boozer lowers his shoulder on a drive to the rim and plows over UConn guard Silas Demary Jr.HALF: Duke 44, UConn 29The swarming Duke defense has cornered the Huskies into 1-for-11 shooting from 3-point range.Cameron (14 points) and Cayden (13 points) Boozer starred in the first half for Duke, which once commanded a 19-point lead.Tarris Reed Jr. leads UConn with 12 points. Alex Karaban, who averaged 22 points per game in the first three rounds, has 0 points, 0 rebounds and 0 assists in 16 minutes.Play under reviewDuke 44, UConn 27 -- 53 seconds first half: An offensive foul on Duke's Caleb Foster on an inbounds play is under review for a flagrant foul. It remained a common foul.Malachi Smith, a key contributor for UConnDuke 44, UConn 27 -- 53 seconds first half: The transfer guard from Dayton crashes with Duke defender Dame Sarr in the paint and drops in a layup. UConn's sixth man is up to 7 points for the game.Cayden Boozer on a roll for DukeDuke 44, UConn 25 -- 3:30 first half: The crafty point guard converts consecutive layups in transition to prop up a 19-point lead for the Blue Devils. Cayden Boozer has 13 points on 4-for-4 shooting from the field.Scoring drought for UConnDuke 38, UConn 21 -- 5:30 first half: The Huskies have now gone over four minutes without a field goal. Tarris Reed Jr. (12 points) heads to the bench after picking up his second foul. The Blue Devils are on a 12-0 run.Dame Sarr hits another 3-pointer for DukeDuke 35, UConn 21 -- 6:45 first half: Duke's Cameron Boozer fires a cross-court pass to the open shooter Sarr, who knocks down his second 3-pointer. He has 8 points for the game. The Blue Devils are on a 9-0 run.Boozer's defense leads to Boozer's offense for DukeDuke 30, UConn 21 -- 7:29 first half: Duke's Cameron Boozer emphatically rejects a shot inside by UConn's Tarris Reed Jr., setting up a transition opportunity for his twin brother, Cayden, to be fouled attacking the rim.Cameron Boozer, Duke have 10-point leadDuke 26, UConn 16 -- 10:02 first half: Duke's Caleb Foster finds Boozer for a right-handed hook along the baseline as the Blue Devils assert a double-digit cushion.Tarris Reed Jr. is a go-to option for UConnDuke 22, UConn 16 -- 13:00 first half: The senior center flips up consecutive layups inside for UConn. He has 12 of the Huskies' first 16 points.Braylon Mullins hits floater for UConnDuke 19, UConn 12 -- 13:50 first half: The freshman guard probes the baseline and softly pushes a right-handed floater up and through. It's his first field goal of the game.Cameron Boozer is on the board for DukeDuke 14, UConn 6 -- 15:30 first half: A possession after Dame Sarr hits from downtown, Cameron Boozer receives a lob pass and finishes with a layup.Isaiah Evans is on target early for DukeDuke 7, UConn 2 -- 17:30 first half: The hot-handed sophomore guard gets his first look to drop from deep. Evans had 25 points in the Blue Devils' previous game vs. St. John's.UConn men's basketball vs. Duke injury reportBoth teams will put forth their usual rotations in Sunday's matchup. Duke's Ifeanyi Ufochukwu, a reserve sophomore center, is the lone player on either injury report, however, due to the season-ending knee injury he suffered during practice earlier this year.How to watch UConn vs Duke in March Madness basketballTV: CBSAnnouncers: Ian Eagle (play-by-play), Bill Raftery (analyst), Grant Hill (analyst), Tracy Wolfson (reporter)Radio: WICH-Norwich (1310 AM, 94.5 FM), WILI-Willimantic (1400 AM, 95.3 FM), Fox Sports (97.9 FM Hartford), UConn Sports Network, WAVZ-New Haven (1300 AM), WGCH-Greenwich (1490 AM).Radio announcers: Mike Crispino (play-by-play), Wayne Norman (analyst)Live stream: FUBO, SLING Satellite radio: SiriusXM: 208 or 201WestwoodOneSports.com: Scott Graham (play-by-play), Tom Crean (analyst)Names to knowCameron Boozer, Duke: This standout freshman projects to be one of the picks in the NBA Draft this June. He posted a double-double of 22 points and 10 rebounds vs. St. John's in the Sweet Sixteen.Alex Karaban, UConn: The senior stretch-four has had a hot hand all tournament. After putting up a career-high 27 vs. UCLA in the Sweet Sixteen, Karaban buried three 3-pointers to reach 17 points vs. Michigan State in the Elite Eight.Tarris Reed Jr., UConn: The senior center is averaging 20.3 points and 15 rebounds in three tournament games, which is inflated by a 31-point, 27-rebound opener vs. Furman.Isaiah Evans, Duke: Sophomore swingman willed the Blue Devils to a win over St. John's last time out, pouring on a game-high 25 points and four 3-pointers.UConn vs Duke gambling oddsDuke vs. UConn odds as of 3 p.m. on Sunday, via BetMGM.Moneyline: Duke (-220); UConn (+180)Spread: Duke (-5.5)Over/under total: 133.5
